category_title: Students who internalize school-ascribed negative labels despite high engagement in elective contexts
minimal_context: The student is asked to complete a required reading assignment and answer comprehension questions within a specific time limit in a traditional English class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please read this assigned text and answer the comprehension questions. You have 20 minutes to finish.

STUDENT: I am an avid reader who enjoys reading when it’s not required. When it’s required, I think that it just feels like a chore, something I have to do, and I don’t want to do it.

TUTOR: We need to practice reading quickly and ripping apart the text to find the meaning.

STUDENT: I’m a really slow reader, and I have a lot of issues with reading, so when I have a specific time, it puts more pressure on me and makes it a lot more difficult for me to read.

TUTOR: Just try your best to get through the questions.

STUDENT: (Refuses to complete the required reading) The reading parts, I suffer in ‘cause I just don’t like school reading. I never read for English.

options.A: Continuously remind the student to show effort and participate, even if they do not know the answers.
options.B: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the assigned reading and answering the comprehension questions.
options.C: Emphasize student self-selection of all reading texts and an individualized approach to reading assessment.
options.D: Implement an in-class reward system where the student earns a sticker for completing the reading target.
